title: Govt. and pvt. sector align on PPPs to secure future of Sri Lankan healthcare
byline: The Sri Lankan government has signaled a strong commitment to expanding public-private partnerships (PPPs) within the healthcare sector, aligning with industry leaders who view collaborative governance as the key to unlocking the country’s medical potential.

title: UN research vessel to conduct marine survey in Sri Lankan waters
byline: The United Nations-flagged research vessel R/V Dr. Fridtjof Nansen is scheduled to arrive in Sri Lanka today to carry out a marine scientific survey in the country’s Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).

title: Drought affects tea cultivation
byline: The prevailing dry weather has severely affected tea cultivation in the central hills much to the anxiety of the planters and the tea smallholders.

title: Panic buying led to premature fuel price increase – CPC Chairman
byline: While urging the public to limit fuel consumption, Chairman of the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation D. J. Rajakaruna said the recent rise in fuel prices had been significantly influenced by panic buying, with many consumers purchasing fuel in large quantities over the past few days due to fears of a possible shortage.

title: YouTube opens deepfake detection tool to politicians and journalists
byline: YouTube on Tuesday started offering a free tool to government officials, journalists and political candidates to help them identify and remove AI-generated videos that resemble their appearance.

title: Death penalty, life imprisonment introduced for high seas drug crimes
byline: A gazette has been issued officially enacting new legislation that introduces severe penalties—including the death penalty and life imprisonment—for drug-related crimes committed on the high seas.

title: Sallay running rat fever risk: MP
byline: Former State Intelligence Services (SIS) Chief Suresh Sallay who is under detention order is running a risk of being infected with rat fever, Opposition MP Dayasiri Jayasekara said yesterday.

title: Cabraal denies paying Rs. 1.84 Billion in Greek Bond case
byline: Former Central Bank Governor Ajith Nivard Cabraal has refuted recent social media claims suggesting that he paid Rs. 1.84 billion in connection with the controversial Greek bond case.

title: A 1,300-pound Nasa spacecraft to re-enter Earth’s atmosphere
byline: A more than1,300-pound (600kg) Van Allen Probe spacecraft is expected to re-enter Earth’s atmosphere almost 14 years after its launch, Nasa says.

title: Children’s drugs in shortage? Health authorities break silence
byline: Amid concerns among parents about a shortage of medicines for children, the health authorities have denied that there is any serious shortage at the hospitals.

title: Pope Leo fires San Diego bishop accused of stealing $250,000
byline: Pope Leo has accepted the resignation of a Catholic bishop in ​San Diego who was arrested by ‌local authorities on suspicion of stealing $250,000 from his congregation, the Vatican announced on Tuesday.

title: Government rules out shutdown of economic activities over fuel prices
byline: While some countries are taking various measures to reduce fuel consumption amidst sky-rocketing fuel prices due to the tension in the Middle East, Cabinet Spokesman Minister Nalinda Jayatissa said yesterday Sri Lanka is not expecting to reduce fuel consumption by contracting economic activities.

title: US says it destroyed 16 Iranian mine-laying boats near Hormuz strait
byline: The US said it took out more than a dozen mine-laying Iranian vessels Tuesday, and the Islamic Republic vowed to block the region’s oil exports, saying it would not allow ’’even a single liter’’ to be shipped to its enemies.

title: Electricity workers warned to return to duty immediately
byline: Employees involved in maintaining Sri Lanka’s national electricity transmission system have been instructed to report to duty immediately, warning that failure to do so would be treated as a serious disciplinary offence.

title: SLFFA announces leadership transition to guide Sri Lanka’s logistics sector
byline: The Sri Lanka Logistics & Freight Forwarders Association (SLFFA) has announced a transition in its leadership with effect from 6 March 2026.

title: Violating restaurant owner’s FR: SC orders seven Excise Officers to pay Rs. 525,000
byline: The Supreme Court today ruled that the Fundamental Rights of a restaurant owner in Midigama had been violated by seven officers of the Department of Excise and ordered them to pay compensation from their personal funds.

title: Sri Lankan man exposed himself at asylum seeker hotel after assaulting staff, court hears
byline: A Sri Lankan man exposed himself after assaulting two members of staff at a hotel for asylum seekers, a court has heard.

title: Student dies after collapsing during school marathon
byline: A 15-year-old student has died after collapsing while taking part in a practice run for an inter-house sports meet at a school in Buttala, police said.

title: Two day debate on Middle East conflict next week
byline: Party leaders decided to take up a two day debate on the Middle East conflict on March 19 and 20, the Parliament Media Unit confirmed today.

title: Six dead and five injured in ’deliberate’ Swiss bus fire
byline: At least six people have died in a bus blaze in Switzerland, which was allegedly started by a man inside the vehicle, according to police and local media reports.

title: Sri Lanka should play lead role in ensuring security of Indian ocean: G.L.
byline: Sri Lanka should play a lead role in ensuring the security of the Indian Ocean in the wake of the conflict in the Middle East by using the Colombo Security Conclave, former foreign affairs minister G.L. Peiris said today.

title: PM Amarasuriya meets ADB officials in Manila
byline: Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya met senior officials of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) at its headquarters in Manila, Philippines, yesterday (March 10), to discuss strengthening development cooperation between Sri Lanka and the multilateral lender.

title: Police launch CID probe into Madush killing
byline: The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has begun an investigation into the shooting death of underworld gang leader Makandure Madush, who was killed by two unknown gunmen while in the custody of the Colombo Crimes Division in 2020.

title: Kim Jong Un, daughter watch North Korea’s cruise missile tests
byline: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and his teenage daughter observed tests of strategic cruise missiles fired from a warship, state media reported on Wednesday (March 11, 2026), as North Korea threatened responses to U.S.-South Korean military drills.

title: Leptospirosis cases rise in Sri Lanka
byline: Sri Lanka has reported around 13,000 cases of leptospirosis (rat fever) within a year, with nearly 300 deaths recorded, according to the Health Promotion Bureau.

title: India’s Supreme Court allows passive euthanasia in landmark ruling
byline: In a landmark first for India, the Supreme Court has permitted the withdrawal of artificial life support for a 32-year-old man who has been in a coma for more than 12 years.

title: Iran’s new supreme leader ‘safe and sound’ despite war injury reports — president’s son
byline: Iran’s new supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei is “safe and sound” despite reports of an injury on the opening day of US-Israeli strikes on the country, says the son of Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.

title: Facebook-owner buys ’social media network for AI’ Moltbook
byline: Meta, the owner of Instagram and Facebook, has bought Moltbook, a social media networking platform for artificial intelligence (AI) bots to speak to each other.

title: Afghanistan’s white-ball series against Sri Lanka postponed
byline: The Afghanistan Cricket Board (ACB) announces that the Afghanistan vs Sri Lanka bilateral series, originally scheduled to commence on 13 March in the United Arab Emirates, has been rescheduled to the last quarter of 2026 due to logistical challenges, including flight constraints arising from the ongoing regional situation.

title: Court orders handover of bodies of 84 Iranian sailors to embassy
byline: The Chief Magistrate of Galle, Sameera Dodangoda, has ordered the Director of Galle National Hospital to hand over the bodies of 84 Iranian sailors currently kept at the hospital to officials of the Embassy of Iran in Sri Lanka.

title: Bakery product prices remain unchanged
byline: The All Ceylon Bakery Owners Association says bakeries across the country are facing difficulties obtaining key energy sources such as diesel, petrol, kerosene and gas, but there are no plans to increase bakery product prices at present.

title: SriLankan Airlines to increase Melbourne flights to 10 per week
byline: SriLankan Airlines has announced plans to increase its weekly flights between Colombo and Melbourne to 10 services, effective from August 2, in response to growing travel demand.

title: CTB bus stolen by private bus conductor
byline: A private bus conductor was arrested last morning by Bandarawela Police on suspicion of stealing a SLTB bus which had been parked at the Bandarawela main bus stand for the night.

title: Heat Index to reach ‘caution level’ in several areas today
byline: The Department of Meteorology has warned that the heat index, the temperature felt on the human body, is likely to increase to ‘Caution Level’ in several parts of the country today(11), the Meteorology Department said.

title: YouTube opens deepfake detection tool to politicians and journalists
byline: YouTube on Tuesday started offering a free tool to government officials, journalists and political candidates to help them identify and remove AI-generated videos that resemble their appearance.

title: LAUGFS Gas increases domestic LPG refill prices from tonight
byline: LAUGFS Gas PLC has announced a revision of domestic Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) refill prices with effect from midnight today (11).

title: Iran tells world to get ready for $200 a barrel
byline: Iran’s military command said on Wednesday the world should be prepared for oil to hit $200 a barrel, as three more ships came under attack in the blockaded Gulf.

title: Namal calls for credible investigation into Easter Sunday attacks
byline: Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa says the investigation into the 2019 Easter Sunday Attacks should be carried out in a fair and transparent manner without being influenced by political rivalries or geopolitical agendas.

title: CSE Slips Marginally as Profit-Taking Weighs on Market
byline: The Colombo market closed slightly lower on 11th March 2026, as profit-taking and the absence of notable block trades led to a volatile trading session. The market traded in positive territory during the first half of the session, but gradually declined toward the close as selling pressure emerged. Overall market activity remained relatively subdued, with both turnover and share volumes staying moderate.

title: Retired auditor released on bail in asset case
byline: Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragamage today ordered that U.K. Sumanasekara, retired auditor of the Department of Civil Security, who had been taken into custody by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption over alleged illicit asset accumulation, be released on bail.

title: Electricity trade unions call off strike
byline: The electricity trade unions have called off their strike action, which was launched following the dissolution of the Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB).

title: SC reserves judgment in carrom board case
byline: The Supreme Court today reserved its judgment in the appeals filed by former Sports Minister Mahindananda Aluthgamage and former Lanka Sathosa Chairman Nalin Fernando, challenging the legality of the High Court judgment that convicted and sentenced them in connection with the controversial carrom board case.

title: Court steps in over fertilizer smell complaints
byline: The Colombo Additional Magistrate H.D.D.J. Premaratne has directed the Peliyagoda Public Health Inspector to conduct a full investigation and submit a report to court regarding complaints that the use of leftover fish from the Peliyagoda Manning Market in fertilizer production by a private company has caused nuisance to local residents.

title: Guilty of unhygienic food handling, five hotel owners fined
byline: Five hotel owners operating within the Manning Market Complex in Peliyagoda were today fined a total of Rs. 125,000 by the Colombo Additional Magistrate H.D.D.J Premaratne, for maintaining food in unhygienic conditions and selling food unfit for human consumption.

title: Two drones fall near Dubai airport, four injured
byline: Dubai authorities have confirmed that two drones fell in the vicinity of Dubai International Airport (DXB) on Wednesday morning, resulting in minor injuries to two Ghanaian nationals and one Bangladeshi national, and moderate injuries to one Indian national. Air traffic is operating as normal.

title: Cricket body rejects bias claims over post-World Cup travel delays
byline: Cricket’s governing body Wednesday rejected suggestions of unequal treatment after the West Indies and South Africa squads were stranded in India for more than a week following the T20 World Cup, with both now finally starting to fly out.

title: Three ships in Strait of Hormuz hit by ’unknown projectiles’
byline: Three cargo vessels have been hit by ’’unknown projectiles’’ in the Strait of Hormuz, maritime authorities say, as pressure intensifies on one of the world’s most important shipping lanes.

title: Spain permanently withdraws ambassador as rift with Israel deepens
byline: Spain permanently withdrew its ambassador to Israel on Tuesday as a ​diplomatic standoff worsened between the two countries ‌over Spain’s opposition to the U.S.-Israeli attacks on Iran.
